chapter.twelfth_labor.title: Heracles and Cerberus
chapter.twelfth_labor.intro: Heracles, son of Zeus and Alcmene, opens the age of heroes. His adventure with Cerberus is the one labour that appears in a literary text of his own time. Hades rules the underworld, and the Erinyes pursue those who wrong their own kin.
chapter.ragnarok.title: Ragnarok: The Wolf Breaks Free
chapter.ragnarok.intro: In Norse myth, Ragnarok is the end of the world, when the wolf Fenrir breaks his chains and battles the gods.
chapter.weighing_heart.title: The Weighing of the Heart
chapter.weighing_heart.intro: In Egyptian belief, the heart of the dead was weighed against the feather of Ma'at. Ammit devoured the hearts of those found unworthy.

chapter.monster_slayers.title: Slayers of Monsters
chapter.monster_slayers.intro: In the age of heroes, Theseus goes to Crete to slay the Minotaur, whom Pasiphae gave birth to. Perseus slays Medusa, and the Chimera is slain by heroes such as Perseus and Bellerophon.
chapter.trojan_war.title: The Trojan War
chapter.trojan_war.intro: The abduction of Helen starts the Trojan War. Achilles kills Penthesilea and Memnon, and Paris kills Achilles. Sinon persuades the Trojans to take the horse in, and sea-serpents kill the priest Laocoon, who tried to destroy it.
chapter.titanomachy.title: The War of the Titans
chapter.titanomachy.intro: Cronus, the youngest Titan, overthrew his father Uranus. Zeus, son of Cronus and Rhea, won the war against the Titans, helped by the Cyclopes whom he freed from Tartarus.
